html:
A telegraph line about 3,200 kilometres long, built from 1870 to 1872 across the middle of Australia from Adelaide to Darwin. It linked Australia to the world's telegraph network.

South Australia won the race to connect with an undersea cable coming from Java. Its postmaster Charles Todd ran the project. The route followed the path of explorer John McDouall Stuart, who had crossed the continent in 1862. Crews dragged wooden and iron poles through desert and tropical floods, and set up repeater stations along the way. One of them grew into Alice Springs.

The line was finished in August 1872 and joined to the Java cable soon after. News from London, which had come by ship in two or three months, now arrived in hours. Like the transatlantic cable a few years earlier, it shrank the world. For a far colony of the British Empire it meant faster prices for wool and gold and closer ties to Britain, and it opened the interior of Australia to cattle stations.
sum: A telegraph line about 3,200 kilometres long, built from 1870 to 1872 across the middle of Australia from Adelaide to Darwin. It linked Australia to the world's telegraph network.
